body:
# Independent audit: zero-face lattice projection and continuous rank

Audited source:
`candidate 1d07780671b93642`.


is required. The source was read in full. This audit specifically does
not authorize summing its overlapping face restrictions as a partition.

## 1. Canonical zero face and lattice projection

The canonical hull is the convex hull of a finite union of compact
sampled fibers; it is compact, and each of its points is a finite convex
combination of points of those fibers. The affine majorant A is
nonnegative on the entire hull. A convex combination has A value zero
only if each positive-weight constituent has A value zero. This proves
the exact generating identity for F and then B=conv Z_F.

If z is an integer point of B, a point of F projects to z. The projection
of the canonical hull is conv P, and lattice completeness puts z in P.
Thus that nonempty zero fiber is one of the sampled fibers and belongs
to Z_F. The converse is immediate. Hence B is a lattice polytope with
precisely the asserted sampled integer support. No lattice point is
being inferred from a continuous projection without a fiber lift.

The continuous gradient of A cannot vanish: a nonempty canonical zero
face has a sampled zero fiber by the generating identity, and then an
affine function depending only on the base would vanish on that entire
positive fiber. This contradicts A>=L>0 in its interior.

## 2. Reciprocal integrability excludes sampled zero facets

A zero face of dimension d-1 in a positive fiber contains a relative
(d-1)-ball. Coning that ball to an interior point gives sections at
small positive A levels with a uniform positive (d-1)-measure. Ordinary
coarea for the nonzero continuous gradient therefore makes the integral
of 1/A diverge as integral_0^epsilon ds/s. Since 1/L>=1/A wherever
positive and the cone lies in the fiber, this contradicts the exact
reciprocal integrability assumption. A d-dimensional zero fiber is
already excluded by interior positivity. Thus every nonempty sampled
zero fiber has dimension at most d-2.

For d=1 the same argument uses a point face and a nontrivial interval
cone, so every endpoint zero is excluded. The d=0 case is excluded by
positive sampled values and the canonical zero-face generating identity.
The source does not apply an undefined negative-dimensional coarea
formula in these cases.

## 3. Relative-interior fiber dimension

The source's proof of

    dim D_z=dim D-dim projection(D), z in relint projection(D),

is valid. A relative interior point of D projects into the relative
interior of its projection because the linear projection maps a relative
ball onto a set containing a relative neighborhood. Any other relative
interior projected point can be reached by a strict convex combination
of that anchor and a lifted point farther along the ray. The scaled
relative ball at the resulting lift remains inside D. Intersecting it
with the vertical affine kernel proves the lower dimension bound, and
the affine-hull kernel gives the matching upper bound. If the projected
point equals the initial anchor, the first relative ball already proves
the conclusion.

For F the vertical kernel lies in the kernel of the nonzero continuous
gradient of A, so it has dimension at most d-1. If that dimension equals
d-1, an integer point in relint B would contradict Section 2. When F
is a relative facet of the canonical hull of dimension r+d, the exact
dimension inequality forces dim B=r and vertical dimension d-1.
Therefore its projected relative interior is lattice-free, as claimed.

## 4. Maximal sampled faces and the exact parity bound

Every lattice point z of the polytope B belongs to the relative interior
of its unique minimal face E(z). The finite inclusion-maximal members
therefore cover all sampled bases, and each contains an integer point
in its relative interior.

Because B is generated by integer points, V=lin(B-B) has a rank-k
lattice Lambda_B=V intersect Z^n, where k=dim B. Choosing an integer
anchor gives the entire affine lattice of aff B. Points in one class
modulo 2 Lambda_B have an integer midpoint in B. Any face containing
that midpoint contains both endpoints: its nonnegative supporting
affine functional has zero average only when both endpoint values
are zero. Hence the midpoint's minimal face contains the two endpoints'
minimal faces.

If the endpoints lie in relative interiors of two distinct maximal
sampled faces, this is an actual larger member of the same E(z) family,
contradicting maximality. Thus their relative-interior parity sets are
disjoint. Since every such set is nonempty and Lambda_B/2 Lambda_B has
2^k classes, there are at most 2^k maximal sampled faces.

This proves exactly the source's relative-interior assertion. The full
faces can meet along boundaries; those boundaries can contain lattice
points and can share parities. There is no lower bound of 2^(dim E)
for the number of relative-interior parity classes of a face.

## 5. Continuous affine rank of each restriction

An exposed base functional for E_l pulls back to an exposed face F_l
of F, with projection exactly E_l. At an integer point z_l in relint
E_l, the fiber of F_l is the original zero fiber F_zl. The dimension
formula from Section 3 and the sampled-facet exclusion give

    dim F_l-dim E_l=dim F_zl<=d-2.

No general-position or full-dimensionality assumption on F_l is being
used. If E_l=B, the base functional can be identically zero and the
restriction is simply F. If F is a zero facet, the absence of a
relative-interior integer point in B makes all E_l proper, so their
base dimensions also drop. The case k=0 is included; its sole face is
a point and its integer fiber has dimension at most d-2.

## 6. Iterated convex-hinge localization

For fixed j, the globally defined function

    [f-i A-j B_l]_+

is nonnegative finite convex. On the actual limiting physical support,
A>=0. As i increases it decreases to [f-j B_l]_+ on F and zero
elsewhere, with a finite bound depending on that fixed j. Applying the
already proved directional payment to these tests and passing the limit
therefore restricts it exactly to F.

On F, the base functional B_l is nonnegative. The subsequent j limit
decreases to f on F_l and zero on its complement in F, bounded by f.
All pointwise inverse-rate measures are finite for a positive rate,
and the integrated reserve has finite mass by its surface-tail identity.
Dominated convergence thus applies to every term for either canonical
right or left rate limit. This proves the exact restricted payment
without a parity factor or a change in beta.

The order of the limits is important: B_l may be negative away from F.
The source takes the order that gives a valid dominating function at
each stage. It does not pretend that [f-j B_l]_+ alone localizes on the
unrestricted canonical body.

## 7. Explicit nonconclusions

The finite family F_l covers the sampled zero set, not necessarily all
of the continuous exposed face F. The actual defect measures live on
the sampled set, so the cover is sufficient to find a nonzero restricted
piece if the original defect is nonzero.

These pieces may overlap on sets carrying defect mass. Summing their
payments counts such mass repeatedly; no disjoint partition, total
mass identity, or additive parity budget follows from this cover.
Selecting one positive piece is legitimate; summing it as an exhaustive
disjoint decomposition is not.

Finally the restricted inverse measures can be singular, including
atoms or nonuniform tangential laws. The reduction of continuous affine
rank to at most d-2 does not convert them into the intrinsic uniform
measure of a lower-dimensional convex body. Applying OC or a continuous
Grünbaum theorem to those restrictions requires a separate, presently
unproved measure statement.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
